title: Algorithmic Fairness and Color-blind Racism: Navigating the Intersection

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical analysis applying Bonilla-Silva's frames of color-blind racism (abstract liberalism, naturalization, cultural racism, minimization of racism) to evaluate the discourse, gaps, and methodologies in existing algorithmic fairness research.

Qualitative critique of how intersectionality is interpreted in fairness research, arguing that the field often reduces it to combining identity categories for demographic parity rather than addressing systems of oppression.
